title: L'automne arrive - nos observations
oneGoal: Students will observe and identify signs that autumn is beginning in our environment
decisionPoints: What autumn signs can students see outside our classroom today?
Should we start with outdoor exploration or window observations?
Are students ready for simple weather comparison activities?
progression: Foundation lesson - establishes seasonal observation skills and introduces core autumn vocabulary through direct environmental contact
realWorldConnection: How people notice seasonal changes in their daily lives and prepare for weather changes

title: Les feuilles commencent à changer
oneGoal: Students will observe leaf color changes and understand that this is a natural autumn process
decisionPoints: Which leaf colors are students noticing in our area?
Should we collect real leaves or observe them on trees first?
Are students ready for color-sorting leaf activities?
progression: Builds on Lesson 1 by focusing specifically on leaf changes while practicing observation vocabulary
realWorldConnection: Observing how trees in our neighborhood and parks change colors each fall

title: Pourquoi les feuilles changent-elles?
oneGoal: Students will understand that leaves change colors because they need less sun and water in autumn
decisionPoints: How can we make sun and water needs concrete for young learners?
Should we use plant experiments or simple demonstrations?
Are students ready for basic cause-and-effect discussions?
progression: Builds on Lesson 2 by introducing simple scientific explanations for leaf color changes through hands-on experiences
realWorldConnection: Understanding why plants and trees need different amounts of sunlight throughout the year

title: Collection de feuilles scientifiques
oneGoal: Students will collect, sort, and record autumn leaf observations using scientific methods
decisionPoints: How many different leaf types can students find safely?
Should we focus on colors, shapes, or sizes first?
Are students ready for simple data recording activities?
progression: Builds on Lesson 3 by applying observation skills to create scientific collections while practicing data recording
realWorldConnection: How scientists collect and organize natural specimens to understand patterns

title: Il fait plus froid - mesurer la température
oneGoal: Students will observe that autumn brings cooler temperatures and learn simple temperature measurement
decisionPoints: What temperature tools are appropriate for Grade 1 students?
Should we compare indoor and outdoor temperatures?
Are students ready for simple thermometer readings?
progression: Builds on Lesson 4 by expanding observations to include temperature while introducing measurement tools
realWorldConnection: How temperature changes affect our clothing choices and daily activities

title: Les jours deviennent plus courts
oneGoal: Students will observe that daylight hours decrease in autumn and understand this affects living things
decisionPoints: How can we make daylight changes visible to young students?
Should we track sunset times or use classroom observations?
Are students ready for before-and-after daylight comparisons?
progression: Builds on Lesson 5 by exploring how sunlight changes affect the environment and living things
realWorldConnection: Noticing how we need lights on earlier and play outside less as autumn progresses

title: Les animaux se préparent pour l'hiver
oneGoal: Students will observe how local animals begin preparing for winter through behavior changes
decisionPoints: Which local animals show obvious preparation behaviors?
Should we observe real animals or use photos and videos?
Are students ready for animal behavior prediction activities?
progression: Builds on Lesson 6 by connecting environmental changes to animal responses while introducing winter preparation concepts
realWorldConnection: Observing how squirrels, birds, and other local animals get ready for cold weather

title: Les oiseaux et la migration
oneGoal: Students will understand that some birds fly south for winter and observe migration behaviors
decisionPoints: Which migrating birds can students observe in our area?
Should we focus on why birds migrate or how they migrate?
Are students ready for simple map activities showing bird journeys?
progression: Builds on Lesson 7 by exploring specific animal adaptation (migration) while reinforcing seasonal change concepts
realWorldConnection: Understanding why we see fewer birds in winter and where they go

title: Fourrure d'hiver - les animaux qui restent
oneGoal: Students will observe how animals that stay develop thicker fur or change color for winter protection
decisionPoints: Which local animals show obvious coat changes?
Should we use real animal fur samples or photos for comparison?
Are students ready for before-and-after animal appearance activities?
progression: Builds on Lesson 8 by exploring another animal adaptation strategy while practicing observation and comparison skills
realWorldConnection: Noticing how pets and wild animals look different in fall and winter

title: Expérience: pourquoi la fourrure?
oneGoal: Students will conduct a simple experiment to understand how fur keeps animals warm in cold weather
decisionPoints: What materials can safely demonstrate insulation for Grade 1?
Should we use ice cubes, warm water, or room temperature comparisons?
Are students ready for hypothesis-making before experiments?
progression: Builds on Lesson 9 by conducting hands-on science to understand animal adaptations through experimental learning
realWorldConnection: Understanding why we wear coats and how animal fur works like our winter clothing

title: Nourriture d'automne - récolter et stocker
oneGoal: Students will understand how animals collect and store food for winter when food becomes scarce
decisionPoints: Which food storage examples are most visible to students?
Should we create our own food storage experiment or observe animal behavior?
Are students ready for discussions about food scarcity and abundance?
progression: Builds on Lesson 10 by exploring how animals prepare food resources while connecting to harvest time themes
realWorldConnection: Observing squirrels gathering nuts and understanding why animals must plan ahead

title: Notre jardin d'automne - que se passe-t-il?
oneGoal: Students will observe how garden plants respond to autumn changes and what happens to their growth
decisionPoints: What plants can students observe changing in our school area?
Should we plant autumn vegetables or observe existing garden changes?
Are students ready for plant growth comparisons over time?
progression: Builds on Lesson 11 by applying seasonal change concepts to plant life while practicing garden observation skills
realWorldConnection: Understanding why gardens produce different foods in different seasons

title: Expérience: les graines en automne
oneGoal: Students will conduct experiments to understand how plants create seeds in autumn for next year's growth
decisionPoints: Which seeds are most appropriate for classroom planting experiments?
Should we focus on seed collection or seed planting activities?
Are students ready for discussions about plant life cycles?
progression: Builds on Lesson 12 by conducting plant science experiments while understanding how plants prepare for next year
realWorldConnection: Learning where fruits and vegetables come from and how plants make new plants

title: Notre livre scientifique d'automne
oneGoal: Students will create a class science book documenting all their autumn observations and discoveries
decisionPoints: What format works best for student science documentation?
Should we include drawings, photos, or written observations?
Are students ready for collaborative book creation activities?
progression: Builds on Lesson 13 by synthesizing all learning into scientific documentation while practicing science communication
realWorldConnection: How scientists share their discoveries by writing and drawing what they learn

title: Prédictions: que va-t-il se passer en hiver?
oneGoal: Students will use their autumn observations to make scientific predictions about winter changes (extension)
decisionPoints: Which predictions can students reasonably make based on autumn observations?
Should we focus on weather, animals, or plant predictions?
Are students ready for hypothesis-making based on evidence?
progression: Extension of Lesson 14 - applies learning to make scientific predictions while reinforcing observation skills
realWorldConnection: How understanding autumn changes helps us prepare for and predict winter conditions

title: Automne autour du monde
oneGoal: Students will explore how autumn looks different in various climates and regions (extension)
decisionPoints: Which global autumn examples are most accessible to Grade 1 students?
Should we use photos, videos, or maps to explore different regions?
Are students ready for climate comparison activities?
progression: Extension of Lesson 15 - broadens perspective on seasonal changes while applying observation vocabulary to global contexts
realWorldConnection: Understanding that autumn happens differently around the world but follows similar patterns

title: Expérience: créer de l'automne
oneGoal: Students will design experiments to recreate autumn conditions and observe their effects (extension)
decisionPoints: What autumn conditions can students safely recreate in classroom experiments?
Should we focus on temperature, light, or water changes?
Are students ready for experiment design rather than just following procedures?
progression: Extension of Lesson 16 - advances to experiment design while reinforcing understanding of autumn environmental factors
realWorldConnection: Learning how scientists use controlled conditions to understand natural processes

title: L'automne et les humains
oneGoal: Students will investigate how humans adapt their behaviors and activities for autumn changes (extension)
decisionPoints: Which human autumn adaptations are most visible to students?
Should we focus on clothing, food, or activity changes?
Are students ready for comparing human and animal adaptations?
progression: Extension of Lesson 17 - connects seasonal changes to human behavior while comparing with animal adaptations studied earlier
realWorldConnection: Understanding how our families change their routines, clothing, and activities for autumn weather

title: Présentation scientifique
oneGoal: Students will present their autumn science discoveries to others using scientific language and evidence (extension)
decisionPoints: What format best allows students to share their scientific learning?
Should presentations focus on individual discoveries or group findings?
Are students ready for answering questions about their observations?
progression: Extension of Lesson 18 - culminates learning through scientific communication while practicing presentation skills
realWorldConnection: How scientists share their research with other people to help everyone understand nature better

title: Fête des petits scientifiques d'automne
oneGoal: Students will celebrate their autumn science journey with families by sharing experiments and discoveries (extension)
decisionPoints: How can the celebration showcase each student's scientific growth?
Should we include live experiments or displays of completed work?
What activities best demonstrate student learning to families?
progression: Extension of Lesson 19 - celebrates the complete science unit while building community connections and scientific confidence
realWorldConnection: How sharing our science learning with families helps build community understanding of nature and environmental changes
